title: Career Roadmap · IT Support Technician
summary: An IT Support Technician helps users resolve computer, software, hardware, connectivity and access problems. The role involves installing and configuring devices, diagnosing technical issues, maintaining IT assets, documenting support requests and escalating complex incidents to specialist teams.

facts.Current degree: Diploma in Computer Engineering / Information Technology

about.label: Typical Entry Qualification
about.text: Diploma in Computer Engineering, Information Technology or a related computing discipline

about.label: Work Environments
about.text: IT service companies, corporate offices, educational institutions, hospitals, data centres, government departments and managed service providers

about.label: Career Focus
about.text: Troubleshooting computers, software, networks and user-access issues while maintaining reliable IT operations

blocks.text: An IT Support Technician helps users resolve computer, software, hardware, connectivity and access problems. The role involves installing and configuring devices, diagnosing technical issues, maintaining IT assets, documenting support requests and escalating complex incidents to specialist teams.

A diploma in Computer Engineering or Information Technology provides a relevant foundation for entry-level IT support roles. Candidates can begin as Help Desk Technicians, Desktop Support Technicians, IT Support Trainees or Technical Support Associates and progress toward system administration, networking, cloud support or cybersecurity.
Employers value practical troubleshooting, communication, documentation and the ability to resolve problems efficiently—not just theoretical knowledge.

rows.text: Build computer hardware, operating-system, networking and troubleshooting skills. Enter help desk or desktop support roles.
Handle complex incidents, endpoint management, identity and access issues, and basic system administration.
Specialize in cloud support, network administration, endpoint security, IT operations or infrastructure management.
Potentially progress into IT Operations Manager, Infrastructure Manager, Service Delivery Manager, Cloud Operations Specialist or independent IT consulting.

blocks.text: Progression depends on practical experience, certifications, specialization and employer requirements.
A diploma in Computer Engineering or Information Technology commonly takes three years after Class 10, though duration and curriculum vary by institution.

blocks.text: Follow organizational procedures for privileged access, software installation, remote access and handling user data. Do not bypass security controls to resolve a support issue.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Computer Troubleshooting Lab
Set up a computer or virtual machine and document common problems involving storage, software installation, startup and peripherals.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: hardware diagnosis, operating systems and technical documentation.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Small Office Network Setup
Build a simulated network with multiple devices and practise IP addressing, DNS checks, connectivity testing and basic router configuration.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: networking, troubleshooting and network documentation.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: IT Help Desk Ticket Tracker
Create a simple ticket-tracking application or spreadsheet that records incidents, priorities, assigned technicians, status and resolution notes.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: IT service management, workflow design and reporting.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: IT Support Automation Scripts
Write simple PowerShell or Python scripts to collect device information, check disk space or organize diagnostic logs.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: scripting, system administration and repetitive-task automation.

blocks.text: Certifications can help structure learning and demonstrate foundational knowledge. Choose them according to your target support role and budget.

rows.text: Cisco CCST Networking or Cisco CCNA learning pathway

blocks.text: Certification names, exam availability and prices may change. Check the official provider's current requirements before enrolling. A certificate should complement hands-on practice, not replace it.

blocks.text: By graduation and initial practical training, aim to demonstrate:

blocks.text: computer assembly, component identification and peripheral troubleshooting.

blocks.label: Operating systems
blocks.text: Windows support and basic Linux command-line usage.

blocks.label: Networking
blocks.text: IP addressing, DNS, DHCP, Wi-Fi and basic connectivity diagnosis.

blocks.label: IT operations
blocks.text: ticketing, incident priority, asset management and escalation.

blocks.label: Security
blocks.text: least privilege, safe remote access, patching and phishing awareness.

blocks.label: Automation
blocks.text: introductory PowerShell or Python scripting.

blocks.label: Communication
blocks.text: professional user support and clear documentation.

blocks.label: Portfolio
blocks.text: a troubleshooting lab, network simulation, ticket tracker and automation script.
A strong entry-level candidate should be able to:

items.text: Diagnose common computer hardware and software problems.
Install and configure operating systems and approved applications.
Troubleshoot basic network connectivity and IP configuration.
Manage support tickets and write useful resolution notes.
Apply fundamental cybersecurity and privacy practices.
Assist with user accounts and device management within authorized permissions.
Communicate technical information clearly to non-technical users.
Demonstrate practical experience through projects or an internship.

blocks.label: Recommended path

blocks.text: The strongest candidates combine structured troubleshooting, customer communication, networking fundamentals and security awareness. Start with strong desktop support skills, then specialize in networking, cloud or cybersecurity to expand long-term career options.
